description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
The TMT which provided to Jalal Foundation was mainly in 3 phases:
**The first phase** Training in the field of Training of Trainers (TOT). Organised in Kabul in June 2021. At the first stage we trained a number of participants (5) as instructors to strengthen their facilitation skills so that they can disseminate what they have learned from the TMT to colleagues and stakeholders. The instructors internalized the gained knowledge and redesign the curriculum for their follow -up trainings. This we have done through on-job coaching. The participants enhanced their knowledge and skills in the following areas:
-Training design, delivery and evaluation
-Participatory Training Methods
-Facilitating Group Dynamics
-Communication and Presentation skills
**The second phase **
Training in Effective communication and soft skills. Organised in Kabul in July 2021. we provided a training in the field of communication and soft skills to improve the soft skills of women staff members and activists on their commitment, motivation, and self-esteem while dealing with male members of the society, particularly in the rural areas.
**The third phase **
Training / strategic meeting on UNSCR 1325 on Women, Peace, and Security, and advocacy. Organised in Istanbul October 2022.
The political changes in Afghanistan in 2021 had thrown woman back in their direly achieved changes. Although there were still numerous challenges and barriers for women, as part of conservative and patriarchal cultures in a multi-ethnic country, what is lost is an institutional and governmental framework where changes could be negotiated by organisations, activists and female politicians.
The WPS agenda, based on UNSCR 1325 and following resolutions, has changed in Afghanistan, as there is no government that can be hold accountable for it, given the current regime. But WPS is more than high level and visible processes for peace and development. It always can only be useful when there are conditions in the country, at the level of the position of women. Social and political changes go hand in hand, but based on current situation in Afghanistan our focus in the training was more on social change (in society) than at the political level.
In the meeting we worked on answering the following questions:
What are currently opportunities to act for change? Which institutions at local and national level are accessible? How can women still network and coordinate, in the country and with diaspora and international networks, also to get at the table of ongoing international peace talks?
We treated the following subjects:
UNSCR1325 on WPS (history, definition, concepts and approaches) UNSCR1325 on WPS functions in post-conflict countries and challenges UNSCR 1325 on WPS priorities and challenges in implementing in Afghanistan Advocacy concepts, tools and methods Development and implementation of advocacy strategy/ campaign Communicating complex information effectively through advocacy (clear, concise and quotable)
Furthermore in three groups the participants worked on 3 different messages, resulting in -A joint statement of the group and released on social media and in some media -A draft message and demands on the situation of exiled women in neighbouring countries, including Turkey, for basic services and conditions, to be able earn a living and create opportunities for meeting and acting with activists elsewhere. -A plan to organize a follow up meeting in Ankara, expanding the number of women and concrete actions. Jalal Foundation will start working on it. -Individual commitments and plans at the local level and according to each ones’ possibility and capacity, to build up a movement and one voice, build on different messages. With for instance involving more youth, using art to raise awareness and inform a big public on the situation and ambitions of Afghan women and supporting Afghan students to write and express in English.
Except for concrete learning’s, plans and messages, it must be mentioned that the training/ meeting, the informal conversations and sharing the pain and hope, inspired and empowered all participants to look forward instead of looking back.
